caption: Did Job predict bodily resurrection? Perhaps—but the Hebrew is famously difficult and may describe vindication before death. This claim is too uncertain for confidence.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Job predict resurrection? Job says he will see God after his skin is destroyed. Jesus later says the dead will leave their graves.
slides.body: Job says he will see God after his skin is destroyed. Jesus later says the dead will leave their graves.
slides.heading: Did Job predict resurrection?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Job 19:23-27: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
slides.body: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
slides.heading: Job 19:23-27

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 5:28–29, BSB: All who are in their graves will hear His voice and come out.
slides.body: All who are in their graves will hear His voice and come out.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 5:28–29

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: This can sound like real hope Some translations make Job expect to see God in his body after death, fitting later Christian resurrection belief.
slides.body: Some translations make Job expect to see God in his body after death, fitting later Christian resurrection belief.
slides.heading: This can sound like real hope

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the Hebrew is difficult Job may expect vindication before death, or speak poetically after it. The passage is too uncertain for a confident prediction.
